Filling the M249's 200-round box or Guns of Marz's M60 100-round box takes one belt link per round. Unloading a round gives its link back, and a fired round's link comes out with its casing. Link boxes are found in the M249 and M60 kits and in army ammunition storage, and links can be made from sheet metal. Off = the belt boxes load like any magazine, no link boxes are found and the link recipes are hidden. Links already in the world stay. A change takes effect the next time the game is loaded.
Trigger Pull Lead for Gun Critical Hits

Only used when Gun Critical Hits is set to Enhanced. How strongly the trigger pull's roll pulls the other targets' rolls along, from 0 (each target rolls on its own) to 100 (every target copies the trigger pull). At 50, a target with a 30%% chance crits at 65%% after a critical trigger pull and at 15%% after a plain one, so on average it still crits at its own chance.

How critical hits are decided when one shot hits several targets, such as shotgun pellets or rounds that pierce. A critical hit does at least double damage, knocks a zombie down and makes a head hit more likely. A shot that hits one target is the same under every choice.
Default is the game's own rule since Build 42.22. One roll when the trigger is pulled decides every target, so a shotgun blast crits with every pellet or with none.
Old is the rule from before Build 42.22. Every target rolls at its own chance.
Enhanced lets every target roll, led by the trigger pull. A critical pull raises the other targets' chance and a plain pull lowers it, as far as Trigger Pull Lead for Gun Critical Hits sets, so on average each target still crits at its own chance.

Since Build 42.22, a gun's failed hit roll on a zombie only staggers it and does no damage. This sets how much damage such a hit still does, as a share of what the same hit would have done had it landed. The share applies to the final damage, after the body part hit (a foot takes far less than the head), clothing and range. A failed roll never gets the critical hit bonus.
0 is the game's own rule.
100 makes every hit that reaches a zombie do full damage, the same as Build 42.21. There it came from a bug, which Build 42.22 fixed.
Hits on players and animals are not changed. Nothing changes while Firearms Use Damage Chance is set to Disabled, where a failed roll is a clean miss. Hits from a failed roll still give Aiming experience.
Upright Guns in Modded Attachment Slots

Guns held like a pistol (the MP7s and the P90 of the Post-93 add-on) hang the right way up on every attachment slot that takes rifles, also the slots other mods add, such as Plysken Attachments Reborn's backpack slots. Sawn-off shotguns do the same in every holster slot. Off = only the vanilla back and holster slots turn them, and other mods' slots show them upside down. A change takes effect the next time the game is loaded.

Plain (full metal jacket) .30-06, 7.62x51mm and .308 rounds can pass through a zombie and hit the one behind it in every gun that fires them, as they would in reality. Guns of Marz lets only some of those guns pierce. Soft points never pierce but hit harder, so choosing between them is always a trade-off. Plain .30-30 rounds are flat-nosed soft points in reality (pointed bullets are unsafe in a tube magazine), so they no longer pierce. Off = Guns of Marz's own piercing.
Rack unless a PBS-1 is fitted

The Soviet US subsonic round burns too little powder to work an AK's gas system, so the gun has to be racked by hand after every shot. A PBS-1 suppressor traps gas and raises the pressure in the barrel, which pushes enough gas into the gas port to cycle the gun. The round and the suppressor were made as a pair.
